body:
Pass 27. Ran the matched-arm experiment for Epic 7 - it resolves the question.

Both arms use exactly 4 runs of residuals, differing only in whether the two evaluated runs are included. Result: the z = -9.81 signal effect I reported last pass VANISHES - matched paired diff +0.000158, z = +1.39, versus -0.002028 unmatched. 13x smaller, sign flipped. So it was training-set size (2 vs 4 runs), not evaluation-residual contamination. Matched disjoint signal bias is +0.000008 against a target of 0.020462 - essentially unbiased. That is your criterion 5 answered concretely: evaluator correct, learner starved.

What remains is small and I would not call it established: matched NULL arm shows +0.000190, z = +2.40, 90% CI excluding zero - about 0.9% of the signal target. One seed, 500 reps, one of two arms. Worth logging as a follow-up research question rather than a finding.

Suggested: make the matched design the primary comparison (unmatched is confounded), state the equivalence margin from it - 90% CIs bound provenance to roughly +/-0.0003 - and record the null-arm z as follow-up. Full numbers on the bead, ready to lift.
